case_name: Union Of India & Ors. vs Syed Ahmed
facts_of_case: The respondent was initially appointed as Medical Officer (Unani) in the Central Government Health Scheme w.e.f. January 1987. He approached the Central Administrative Tribunal seeking regularization as Medical Officer (Unani). The Tribunal dismissed his application, and he appealed to this Court.

legal_principles.principle: The period of ad hoc service can be counted towards the purposes of pension under Rule 13 of CCS Pension Rules subject to compliance of Rule 17.
legal_principles.held: In view of the above discussion, we dispose of this OA directing the respondents to consider counting of period of service spent by the applicant on ad hoc basis towards qualifying service in accordance with Rule 3 (1) (q), Rule 13 and Rule 17 of CCS Pension Rules.

legal_principles.principle: The law is clear that the date from which the service was entitled to be counted as qualifying service for fixation of pension is not governed by the DOPT OM dated 1 July 1991.
legal_principles.held: WP(C) 17442/2024 merely observes that the reliance, by the petitioner, on the DOPT OM dated 1 July 1991 was inapt, as the said OM dealt only with regularization of service, and not with the date from which the service was entitled to be counted as qualifying service for fixation of pension.

outcome.final_order: The respondent's service was regularized as Chief Medical Officer on January 2000. He superannuated in March 2016. His pension was fixed based on his qualifying service of 29 years and 3 months.

use_for_drafting: practical application of Code of Civil Procedure
